name: Wurlitzer
description: Wurlitzer electric piano listing copy, organized by production era and catalog model.

children.copy:
Our Wurlitzer restoration process is among the most meticulous in the world, with over 30 hours of expert craftsmanship devoted to every instrument. Throughout our restoration process we prioritize using period-correct vintage components whenever possible, or select the highest quality reproduction parts when necessary. Each restoration is carefully tailored to bring out the very best in the Wurlitzer's action, touch, and iconic tone while remaining true to its original character, earning our highest seal of approval.

Wurlitzers produced during the 110 and 120 eras are known for having a dark, vibey tone with playful, toy-like piano action. During these early years of production, Wurlitzer was still working on improvements to the design of the reeds and the action, but that's not to say they are lacking in charm — these are some of the earliest electric pianos ever made, and some of their more imperfect, honky-tonk attributes are what makes them unique.

Features:
- Fully Restored & Leveled Key Bed
- Comprehensive Action Regulation
- New Jack Springs & Fly Felts
- New Key Bushing Felts
- Improved Electronics Grounding & Shielding
- Warneck Research Variable Vibrato Amplifier
- CEPCo's Expert Tuning & Voicing Setup

Included:
- Legs
- Sustain Pedal
- Music Rack
- Bench

This piano comes from the 140/145 period, where Wurlitzer started to make big strides in the design of the reeds and action. children.label: 140B
children.copy:
Our Wurlitzer restoration process is among the most meticulous in the world, with over 30 hours of expert craftsmanship devoted to every instrument. Throughout our restoration process we prioritize using period-correct vintage components whenever possible, or select the highest quality reproduction parts when necessary. Each restoration is carefully tailored to bring out the very best in the Wurlitzer's action, touch, and iconic tone while remaining true to its original character, earning our highest seal of approval.

This piano comes from the 140B/145B era, when Wurlitzer updated the reeds and action in a way that lasted through the remainder of Wurlitzer electric piano production. These are some of the first "professional" electric pianos, and are beloved by players looking for the darker Wurlitzer tones heard on Motown and Muscle Shoals recordings.

The 140B is the solid-state amplifier model of this era.

Our Wurlitzer restoration process is among the most meticulous in the world, with over 30 hours of expert craftsmanship devoted to every instrument. Throughout our restoration process we prioritize using period-correct vintage components whenever possible, or select the highest quality reproduction parts when necessary. Each restoration is carefully tailored to bring out the very best in the Wurlitzer's action, touch, and iconic tone while remaining true to its original character, earning our highest seal of approval.

This is an early 200-era piano (1968-1970), known for having more grit and bark than later models. These pianos are lighter in weight than the 140B models and were the first to feature the iconic chrome legs and molded plastic tops used for around 15 years of production. Lovers of Donny Hathaway's live recordings will be very pleased with the midrange attack of pianos from this era.

A note on noise: the 200 is often considered noisier than the 200A, but nearly all of the 200A's noise-reduction improvements can be incorporated during restoration. Combined with the installation of a Warneck Research amplifier and additional improvements to grounding, shielding, and lead dress, our restorations achieve a noise floor ready for professional recording and performance.

Our Wurlitzer restoration process is among the most meticulous in the world, with over 30 hours of expert craftsmanship devoted to every instrument. Throughout our restoration process we prioritize using period-correct vintage components whenever possible, or select the highest quality reproduction parts when necessary. Each restoration is carefully tailored to bring out the very best in the Wurlitzer's action, touch, and iconic tone while remaining true to its original character, earning our highest seal of approval.

This is an early 200-era piano (1968-1970), known for having more grit and bark than later models. These pianos are lighter in weight than the 140B models and were the first to feature the iconic chrome legs and molded plastic tops used for around 15 years of production. Lovers of Donny Hathaway's live recordings will be very pleased with the midrange attack of pianos from this era.

A note on noise: the 200 is often considered noisier than the 200A, but nearly all of the 200A's noise-reduction improvements can be incorporated during restoration. Combined with the installation of a Warneck Research amplifier and additional improvements to grounding, shielding, and lead dress, our restorations achieve a noise floor ready for professional recording and performance.

Features:
- Fully Restored & Leveled Key Bed
- Comprehensive Action Regulation
- New Jack Springs & Fly Felts
- New Key Bushing Felts
- Improved Electronics Grounding & Shielding
- Warneck Research Variable Vibrato Amplifier
- CEPCo's Expert Tuning & Voicing Setup

Included:
- Legs
- Sustain Pedal
- Music Rack
- Bench

children.label: 210A
children.copy:
Our Wurlitzer restoration process is among the most meticulous in the world, with over 30 hours of expert craftsmanship devoted to every instrument. Throughout our restoration process we prioritize using period-correct vintage components whenever possible, or select the highest quality reproduction parts when necessary. Each restoration is carefully tailored to bring out the very best in the Wurlitzer's action, touch, and iconic tone while remaining true to its original character, earning our highest seal of approval.

This is a later 200A (1977-1983), from the final years of Wurlitzer production when the tone became much more balanced. These pianos have less transition between the bass, mid, and treble ranges, often with a slightly less percussive attack — which may be preferred by players seeking a smoother Wurlitzer tone.

This model features an 8-inch speaker.
